Description: A biospecimen collected from a new primary malignancy that arose in a patient in addition to a previously diagnosed primary tumor.
A biospecimen derived from an additional metastatic tumor site, collected separately from the first-sampled metastatic lesion.
A substance or chemical constituent extracted or purified from a biospecimen that serves as the target of an analytical procedure, such as a nucleic acid or protein preparation.
A neoplasm that lacks the morphologic features of malignancy, such as severe cytologic atypia or tumor cell necrosis, and remains confined to its site of origin without metastasizing.
The fraction of an anticoagulated blood sample that contains most of the white blood cells and platelets following density gradient centrifugation of whole blood.
A semisolid gelatinous mass of coagulated blood consisting of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets entrapped in a fibrin network.
A bone marrow specimen collected from a subject that has been diagnosed with a hematologic (blood-derived) malignancy.

Attribute: Blood Derived Cancer - Bone Marrow; Post-treatment
Description: A bone marrow specimen collected from a subject with a hematologic malignancy after the subject has received treatment.
A peripheral whole blood specimen collected from a subject that has been diagnosed with a hematologic (blood-derived) malignancy.

Attribute: Blood Derived Cancer - Peripheral Blood; Post-treatment
Description: A peripheral whole blood specimen collected from a subject with a hematologic malignancy after the subject has received treatment.
A blood-based liquid biopsy specimen used to sample circulating tumor cells, cell-free nucleic acids, or other tumor-derived material without a solid tissue biopsy.
A peripheral blood specimen collected from a subject that is used as a source of germline (non-tumor) DNA or as a matched normal control for genomic comparisons.
A liquid substance derived from the body, such as blood, urine, cerebrospinal fluid, or pleural effusion, that is collected as a biospecimen.
A bone marrow specimen collected from a subject that does not contain malignant cells and is used as a normal reference sample.
A sample of normal (non-tumor) cells collected by scraping or swabbing the inside of a subject's cheek, commonly used as a source of germline DNA.
The smallest unit of living structure capable of independent existence, composed of a membrane-enclosed mass of protoplasm containing a nucleus or nucleoid.
A biospecimen derived from tissue that developed after a laboratory cell line was implanted and grown in a non-human host organism.
A permanently established cell culture that will proliferate indefinitely given appropriate fresh medium and growth space.
A biospecimen or analyte that is used as a comparator or reference against an experimental sample.
A long, linear, double-stranded polymer of nucleotides attached to a deoxyribose backbone that carries an organism's genetic information; used here to denote a specimen consisting of extracted DNA.
A biospecimen consisting of normal lymphocytes that have been infected in vitro with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and cultured to establish an indefinitely proliferating cell line.
A next generation cancer model that has been expanded using tissue culture or other propagation methods.
A formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue sample derived from tissue isolated from a subject with recurrent disease.
A formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue sample that has been cut on a microtome into a thin section that rolls up on itself, forming a scroll.
Fibroblast cells isolated from a normal (non-malignant) bone marrow specimen.
A DNA specimen that has been amplified using the GenomePlex (Rubicon Genomics) whole genome amplification method.
A type of leukocyte with a multilobed nucleus and cytoplasmic granules, subdivided into eosinophils, basophils, and neutrophils based on the staining properties of their granules.
A sample comprised of cells that were isolated from a human tumor and have not been cultured or expanded.
Neoplasms confined to the site of origin without invasion beyond the basement membrane or into surrounding tissue, such as carcinoma in situ.
A specimen of normal (non-malignant) lymphoid tissue or cells used as a reference or control sample.
A term referring to the clinical or pathologic observation of a tumor extension from its original site of growth to another anatomic site.
A sample comprised of a mixture of cells or clumps of cells, which may have been isolated from normal or tumor tissue, that are maintained together in a suspension culture.

Attribute: Mononuclear Cells from Bone Marrow Normal
Description: A biological sample containing mononuclear cells isolated from a normal (non-malignant) bone marrow specimen.

Attribute: Neoplasms of Uncertain and Unknown Behavior
Description: Neoplasms that, on morphologic grounds, cannot be classified with certainty as benign or malignant.

An approach to cancer modeling that utilizes clinical data as well as the genomic and transcriptomic profiles of the parent tumor, metastases, if present, and case-matched normal tissues from individual patients.

Attribute: Next Generation Cancer Model Expanded Under Non-conforming Conditions
Description: A next generation cancer model that has been expanded using unconventional or non-standard culturing methods.
An indicator that specifies that a biospecimen collection event was not permitted.
Increased amounts of fluid within the pleural cavity, usually caused by lung infections, congestive heart failure, pleural or lung tumors, connective tissue disorders, or trauma.
A biospecimen collected from a subject after treatment with a neoadjuvant therapeutic agent.

Attribute: Primary Blood Derived Cancer - Bone Marrow
Description: A bone marrow specimen collected from a subject at the time of initial diagnosis of a hematologic (blood-derived) malignancy, prior to treatment.

Attribute: Primary Blood Derived Cancer - Peripheral Blood
Description: A peripheral whole blood specimen collected from a subject at the time of initial diagnosis of a hematologic malignancy, prior to treatment.
A tumor specimen collected from the anatomic site where the cancer originated, as opposed to a metastatic or recurrent site.
Tissue derived from a patient's tumor that has been directly implanted and grown in a non-human host organism without prior in vitro culturing.

Attribute: Recurrent Blood Derived Cancer - Bone Marrow
Description: A bone marrow specimen collected from a subject at the time of relapse or recurrence of a hematologic malignancy.

Attribute: Recurrent Blood Derived Cancer - Peripheral Blood
Description: A peripheral whole blood specimen collected from a subject at the time of relapse or recurrence of a hematologic malignancy.
A tumor specimen collected after the reemergence of cancer at the original or a related site following a period of remission.
A genomic DNA specimen that has been amplified from a limited-quantity sample using the REPLI-g (Qiagen) whole genome amplification technology.
A genomic DNA specimen amplified from an ultra-low-input sample using the REPLI-g X (Qiagen) whole genome amplification kit, designed for single-cell or trace-quantity starting material.
A biospecimen created to contain an isolated or enriched ribonucleic acid (RNA) sample.
The watery fluid in the mouth produced by the salivary glands that moistens food to aid digestion and helps protect the mouth against infection.
A biospecimen consisting of a tissue section or cell preparation mounted on a glass slide for microscopic examination.
A specimen of morphologically normal solid tissue collected from a subject, typically used as a matched normal control for a tumor specimen.
An anatomical structure consisting of similarly specialized cells and intercellular matrix, aggregated according to genetically determined spatial relationships, that performs a specific function.
A biological sample comprised of all of the RNA collected from an experimental subject.
An abnormal mass of tissue that results from excessive cell division; used broadly to denote a neoplasm, which may be benign or malignant.

Attribute: Tumor Adjacent Normal - Post Neo-adjuvant Therapy
Description: A specimen of morphologically normal tissue collected from the area immediately surrounding a tumor, obtained from a subject after treatment with a neoadjuvant therapeutic.
Referring to the entire body of an experimental animal; used when a biospecimen consists of or is derived from an entire organism.
Blood that has not been separated into its various components, other than the addition of an anticoagulant.
Tissue derived from human or animal cells or tumor material that has been transplanted into and grown within a different (non-human) host organism.
Not known, observed, recorded; or reported as unknown by the data contributor.
Not provided or available.
